title: The CSS Box Model: Everything is a Rectangle 📦
description: Understand content, padding, border, and margin – the layers that wrap every element.

slides.title: The Web’s Secret Geometry 🧊
slides.content:
# Every Element is a Box

In CSS, every element is treated as a rectangular box. The **box model** describes the space an element takes up:

- **Content** – the actual text, image, or child elements.
- **Padding** – transparent area around the content, inside the border.
- **Border** – a line surrounding the padding (and content).
- **Margin** – transparent area outside the border, separating the element from others.

Think of it like a framed picture: the photo is content, the mat is padding, the frame is border, and the space to the next frame is margin.

slides.title: Visualising the Box Model
How Big is the Box? 📐
slides.content:
# Total Element Size

By default (`box-sizing: content-box`), the `width` and `height` apply only to the **content area**. Padding and border are added on top.

So the total rendered width = `width + padding-left + padding-right + border-left + border-right`.

In the example above: 200 (content) + 40 (padding) + 10 (border) = 250px actual width.

Margins are outside, they don't count toward the element's size but affect layout.

quizData.question: With `box-sizing: content-box; width: 100px; padding: 10px; border: 5px;` what is the actual rendered width?
quizData.explanation: Content is 100px, plus 10px padding left + right, plus 5px border left + right = 130px.

slides.title: The Box Model in DevTools 🛠️
slides.content:
# Inspect to Understand

Right‑click any element → Inspect. In the **Computed** or **Layout** tab you'll see a diagram of the box model showing content, padding, border, and margin with exact sizes.

This is the #1 debugging tool for spacing issues. Learn to love it.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Everything is Boxes

Even inline elements like `<a>` or `<span>` follow a box model, but vertical margins/paddings behave differently. We'll cover that with the inline model later.
